disease_label_per_paper: Salmonella Typhi-induced septic shock and acute respiratory distress syndrome
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 16-year-old male US resident with no travel abroad presented with a 2-day history of abdominal pain, melanotic diarrhea, and fever.
On admission he was ill appearing, moderately dehydrated, diffusely tender, tachycardic, and initially well perfused.

Within 12 hours, blood cultures grew a gram-negative rod and he was started on IV ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin; the isolate was confirmed as Salmonella Typhi and was susceptible to ampicillin, TMP-SMX, ceftriaxone, azithromycin, and ciprofloxacin.
Hospital day 2 brought fulminant ARDS with severe hypoxemia, diffuse bilateral infiltrates, intubation, and hypotension refractory to fluids requiring vasopressors for 24 hours.
CT later showed ileal enteritis and severe ascites without perforation. He improved after active antibiotics, ICU support, and high-dose dexamethasone adjunct therapy.

Contrasted abdominal computed tomography revealed thickened bowel wall with ileal enteritis and severe ascites, but no perforation.

quality_warnings: Salmonella Typhi speciation and susceptibility are stored in microbiology/confirmatory_findings or treatment-context axes, not as ordinary diagnosis evidence.
The report does not provide numeric admission temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, PaO2/FiO2, creatinine, AST/ALT, or CRP, so those values are not invented.
ARDS and shock are represented as event hazards because the paper reports severe hypoxemia, diffuse infiltrates, intubation, vasopressors, and ICU course without exact numeric vitals.
